## 1. Historical Context

### Early Foundations (1960s-1970s)

| Year | Contributor | Contribution |
|------|-------------|--------------|
| 1960s | Bryson, Ho | Applied the chain rule to optimal control problems |
| 1970 | Seppo Linnainmaa | Independently discovered backpropagation in his master's thesis ("The representation of the cumulative rounding error of an algorithm as a Taylor expansion of individual evaluations") |
| 1974 | Paul Werbos | Proposed backpropagation for neural networks in his PhD thesis |
| 1986 | Rumelhart, Hinton, Williams | Published "Learning representations by back-propagating errors" — the paper that popularized backprop |

### The Deep Learning Revolution (2010s-Present)

### Why Backpropagation Was Revolutionary

Before backpropagation, neural networks were trained using:
- Hebbian learning ("neurons that fire together, wire together")
- Perceptron learning rule
- Linear discriminant analysis

Backpropagation enabled:
- Efficient computation of gradients for arbitrary network architectures
- Training of multi-layer networks
- Automatic feature learning

## 2. The Forward Pass

### Network Architecture

Consider a simple feedforward network:

```
Input Layer    Hidden Layer    Output Layer
    │               │               │
    ▼               ▼               ▼
  [x₁, x₂] ───→ [h₁, h₂, h₃] ───→ [y₁, y₂]
    │               │               │
    │   W¹         │   W²          │
    │  (2×3)       │  (3×2)        │
    ▼               ▼               ▼
  Layer 1         Layer 2         Layer 3
```
